summary: Weston County lookout built in 1940-41 and dismantled in 1966; its steel tower went to Seth Bullock Lookout in South Dakota, where sources disagree on what remains.

facts.design: 45-foot wooden L-4 tower, replaced by 1957 with a 53-foot all-steel live-in tower (firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1966 and taken to Seth Bullock Lookout, Black Hills, South Dakota. No source describes what remains at the Wyoming site.

staffing.status: staffed through the 1965 season; last named lookout LeNora Sundstrom

corrections.why: The tower was dismantled in 1966 and taken to Seth Bullock Lookout in South Dakota (register and firelookout.com). The Wyoming site lost the structure, not only its use.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register: 1941, built by the CCC. Firelookout.com: 1940 for the wooden tower. A November 1940 newspaper item already names a station on Mt. Pisgah. The story gives both years.
Register lists removal in 1965; the same register page quotes a News-Letter Journal item dated September 15, 1966, describing the dismantling. The story gives both dates.

The register and firelookout.com say the Pisgah steel still stands at Seth Bullock. The NHLR dates the current 55-foot tower to 1975, and a Black Hills blog says the tower was rebuilt. The story reports the disagreement and does not settle it.
Firelookout.com gives 53 feet for the Pisgah steel tower and 67 feet after the 1966 move with an added section. The story reports only the 53-foot figure at Pisgah.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' should read 'moved': the steel tower went to Seth Bullock Lookout in Pennington County, South Dakota, in 1966. That South Dakota site is a separate lookout and may need its own record. Build year 1940 vs 1941 is unresolved; the story gives both. Whether any 1957 Pisgah steel stands in the current Seth Bullock tower is disputed between the register, firelookout.com and the NHLR. No source describes the Wyoming summit today, and Wyoming access is unknown. Living New Deal and Facebook or Instagram posts appeared only as search snippets and were not read, so they are not cited. Newspaper items are quoted via westlookouts.weebly.com, which reprints them.
